correctness.rationale: For a path edge, reroot at the target side and use first-step equations: the expected crossing time from the adjacent root-side endpoint equals one plus the sum over its off-target neighbors of one plus their mean return time. Induction on the root-side component size M gives 2M-1; summing gives the forward identity, and commute gives 2ND_N. Every label below b is on the root side of its path edge. The later descent indicators from b either become constantly one or, before that happens, alternate: two zeros are absorbing and cannot reach c_N=1. Each continuation of alternation needs a consecutive second-predecessor choice, so the excess M_b-b is at most L_N+1 (zero at b=N). A union bound on all starting positions and Borel–Cantelli give L_N=O(log N) almost surely, making H⁺−2A_N negligible at scale N^(3/2). Backwards exploration samples previously unseen iid attachment choices at distinct labels; at label 1 the forced final edge preserves all positive labels, so the same bounded-step renewal sequence gives jointly D_N=K_N and A_N=sum of K_x for x=1,…,N in law. A separate enumeration compared the full positive-path profile law and confirmed the deterministic bound for N=1–11 at p=1/2. For the unbounded proof, set K_0=0; the overshoot 0≤S_(K_x)-x≤1 composes the centered partial-sum Donsker process with K_floor(Nt)/N→t/μ uniformly and multiplies it by -1/μ. Brownian scaling then gives -sqrt(v)/μ^(3/2) times standard Brownian motion. Riemann summation and endpoint evaluation give the pair of Brownian functionals ∫B and B(1)−∫B (with common prefactor -2sqrt(v)/μ^(3/2)); their variances are 1/3 and their covariance is 1/6. For the almost-sure conclusion the overshoot yields uniform deviation of K from x/μ bounded by (1+max_(k≤N)|S_k−μk|)/μ. Hoeffding plus a union bound makes linear deviations summably unlikely. Applying this to the fixed-N joint tree laws and then Borel–Cantelli proves the result in the original environment, without a false common renewal coupling across N.
residual_risks: The recorded simulations are diagnostics, not verification of the limiting distribution. The result concerns environment fluctuations of conditional expectations at fixed 0<p<1, not a limit for random walk paths.

evidence: The later indexed proof gives more than a univariate theorem: its cumulative tooth reward C_m has a Brownian FCLT and its infinite forward mean is m²+2 sum_(j≤m) C_j. Those ingredients can be adapted to the finite law: at complete block boundaries σ_m=m+C_m, and within a block the discrepancy is bounded by its size. One must track the inverse birth-label clock jointly with the reward and compare the unfinished-block endpoint and finite mean to the nearest completed ray block. Exponentially tailed blocks have maximal size O(log N), so only O(log N) final edges and at most an O(N log N) mean error need control in that transfer; commute then supplies the reverse coordinate.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is genuine closeness of the mathematical mechanisms, not an exact statement match. The indexed ray proof supports a route after a model-specific random-time and endpoint transfer, rather than a deterministic rescaling of the displayed scalar theorem. Its 2026-11-08 date is later than the frozen finding and does not establish prior coverage. Neither cited earlier primary passage supplies the joint profile and this transfer.

value.rationale: The deterministic commute identity controls only the sum. A joint area-and-endpoint representation resolves the fluctuation split and gives the exact universal half-correlation of the two conditional means at the same finite endpoints. That covariance is useful for joint prediction and directional asymmetry and is not determined by either a scalar ray limit or the commute law alone. The main mechanism is the uniform pathwise control of discarded branches combined with a common inverse-renewal profile.
residual_risks: The method is specific to the two-predecessor model; no downstream limit for general attachment windows or the walk's own hitting-time noise is asserted.
